title: How is Kibana configured in your project, and how does the ELK stack enable centralized logging and request tracing with correlation IDs?
shortTitle: Kibana configuration and how the ELK stack enables centralized logging and request tracing with correlation IDs
keyPoints: ELK is Elasticsearch (stores and indexes logs), Logstash/Beats (collects and ships logs), and Kibana (searches, visualises, and dashboards logs).
Centralized logging ships every microservice's structured JSON logs into one searchable Elasticsearch cluster.
A correlation ID is a unique identifier assigned to each incoming request and propagated to every downstream service call.
In Java, the correlation ID is stored in the MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context), which the logging framework merges into every log line automatically.
In Kibana, filtering by one correlation ID shows the complete journey of a single request across all services.
Never log sensitive data like full account numbers into Elasticsearch; manage index lifecycle for compliance and cost.

s1_definition.oneliner: ELK pools every service's logs into one searchable place, and a correlation ID lets you pull the complete story of a single request out of billions of log lines with one filter.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Elasticsearch** – a distributed search engine that stores each log line as a JSON document in time-based indices and makes them searchable in near-real-time.
- **Logstash / Beats** – agents that collect, parse, and ship logs from every service to Elasticsearch; Filebeat runs as a Kubernetes DaemonSet.
- **Kibana** – a web interface for searching, visualising, and building dashboards over the logs in Elasticsearch.
- **Correlation ID** – a unique identifier assigned to each incoming request at the gateway and propagated in headers to every downstream service, so every log line from one request shares the same ID.
- **MDC (Mapped Diagnostic Context)** – a per-thread map in the Java logging framework that automatically attaches the correlation ID to every log line.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India has fifty branches, each keeping its own paper logbook. When a customer complains about a failed transfer, staff would have to phone every branch and flip through separate books. ELK is like scanning every branch's logbook into one central searchable computer. The correlation ID is like stamping a single reference number on every form a customer's request touches as it moves from the teller to the back office to the vault: type that one number into Kibana and instantly see every step.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Request enters at API Gateway
       │
       │  assigns correlationId = UUID
       ▼
  ┌────────────────────┐  X-Correlation-Id header
  │  Transfer Service  │ ──────────────────────────→
  │  MDC: abc-123-def  │                             │
  │  log: "initiated"  │                             ▼
  └────────────────────┘                 ┌────────────────────┐
                                         │   Fraud Service    │
                                         │   MDC: abc-123-def │
                                         │   log: "check OK"  │
                                         └────────┬───────────┘
                                                   │
                                                   ▼
                                         ┌────────────────────┐
                                         │  Account Service   │
                                         │  MDC: abc-123-def  │
                                         │  log: "debit/credit"│
                                         └────────────────────┘

  All logs ship to Elasticsearch via Filebeat
       │
       ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              Kibana                       │
  │  Filter: correlationId = abc-123-def     │
  │  Result: complete request journey         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
The ELK stack solves the scattered-logs problem in microservices. Elasticsearch stores and indexes logs for fast search, Filebeat ships them from every Pod, and Kibana provides the search and dashboard interface. The real power comes from the correlation ID: a unique identifier assigned at the gateway and propagated to every downstream service via headers and MDC, so every log line from one request shares the same ID.

The payoff is dramatic. When Rajesh reports a failed transfer, the engineer types the correlation ID into Kibana and instantly sees every log line from every service for that one request, in time order. What used to be an hour of cross-referencing across scattered Pods becomes a ten-second filter.

The senior disciplines are: never log sensitive data like full account numbers into Elasticsearch, manage index lifecycle for compliance and cost, and tie the correlation ID to the distributed trace ID so engineers can jump from a slow trace straight to the matching logs.

Remember one sentence: ELK centralizes every service's logs into one searchable place, and the correlation ID is the single key that pulls the complete story of any request out of billions of log lines.
